# dlansf

> Returns the value of the one-norm, Frobenius norm, infinity-norm, or the largest absolute value of any element of a real symmetric matrix stored in Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) format.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlansf from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlansf';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlansf( norm, transr, uplo, N, A, strideA, WORK ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "transpose"` | Specifies the storage format (`'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle is stored (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Input array in RFP format |
| ↳ `strideA` | `integer` | Stride length for `A` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Workspace array, length >= N |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANSF as described above.
- `transr`: Specifies whether the RFP format of A is normal or transposed format.

  -   `= 'N'`: RFP format is Normal;
  -   `= 'T'`: RFP format is Transpose.
- `uplo`: On entry, `UPLO` specifies whether the RFP matrix A came from an upper or lower triangular matrix as follows:

  -   `= 'U'`: RFP A came from an upper triangular matrix;
  -   `= 'L'`: RFP A came from a lower triangular matrix.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANSF is set to zero.
- `A`: On entry, the upper (if `UPLO = 'U'`) or lower (if `UPLO = 'L'`) part of the symmetric matrix A stored in RFP format. See the "Notes" below for more details. Unchanged on exit.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlansf.ndarray(
    norm, transr, uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA, offsetA,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "transpose"` | Specifies the storage format (`'no-transpose'` or `'transpose'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle is stored (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | RFP array of length N\*(N+1)/2 |
| ↳ `strideA` | `integer` | Stride for `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace of length N (only for `'one-norm'`/`'inf-norm'` norms) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride of WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index of WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in DLANSF as described above.
- `transr`: Specifies whether the RFP format of A is normal or transposed format.

  -   `= 'N'`: RFP format is Normal;
  -   `= 'T'`: RFP format is Transpose.
- `uplo`: On entry, `UPLO` specifies whether the RFP matrix A came from an upper or lower triangular matrix as follows:

  -   `= 'U'`: RFP A came from an upper triangular matrix;
  -   `= 'L'`: RFP A came from a lower triangular matrix.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, DLANSF is set to zero.
- `A`: On entry, the upper (if `UPLO = 'U'`) or lower (if `UPLO = 'L'`) part of the symmetric matrix A stored in RFP format. See the "Notes" below for more details. Unchanged on exit.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'` or '1' or 'O'; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: the norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-transpose", "transpose"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlansf from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlansf';

/*
* 3x3 real symmetric matrix in RFP format (upper, no-transpose).
*
* Original symmetric matrix:
*   A = [  4   2   1 ]
*       [  2   5   3 ]
*       [  1   3   6 ]
*
* RFP layout (n=3, upper, no-transpose):
*   Col 0: A(0,1), A(1,1), A(0,0)  = 2, 5, 4
*   Col 1: A(0,2), A(1,2), A(2,2)  = 1, 3, 6
*/
const A = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 5.0, 4.0, 1.0, 3.0, 6.0 ] );
let WORK = new Float64Array( 3 );

let result = dlansf( 'max', 'no-transpose', 'upper', 3, A, 1, WORK );
console.log( 'max norm: %d', result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

WORK = new Float64Array( 3 );
result = dlansf( 'one-norm', 'no-transpose', 'upper', 3, A, 1, WORK );
console.log( 'one-norm: %d', result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

result = dlansf( 'frobenius', 'no-transpose', 'upper', 3, A, 1, WORK );
console.log( 'frobenius norm: %d', result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLANSF`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLANSF returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a real symmetric matrix A in RFP format.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{DLANSF} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(`A(i,j)`)) is not a matrix norm.

### Further Details

We first consider Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) Format when N is even. We give an example where $N = 6$.

```text
AP is Upper             AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04 05       00
   11 12 13 14 15       10 11
      22 23 24 25       20 21 22
         33 34 35       30 31 32 33
            44 45       40 41 42 43 44
               55       50 51 52 53 54 55
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds AP as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid `A(0:5,0:2)` consists of the last three columns of AP upper. The lower triangle `A(4:6,0:2)` consists of the transpose of the first three columns of AP upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid `A(1:6,0:2)` consists of the first three columns of AP lower. The upper triangle `A(0:2,0:2)` consists of the transpose of the last three columns of AP lower. This covers the case N even and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
03 04 05                33 43 53
13 14 15                00 44 54
23 24 25                10 11 55
33 34 35                20 21 22
00 44 45                30 31 32
01 11 55                40 41 42
02 12 22                50 51 52
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'T'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
03 13 23 33 00 01 02    33 00 10 20 30 40 50
04 14 24 34 44 11 12    43 44 11 21 31 41 51
05 15 25 35 45 55 22    53 54 55 22 32 42 52
```

We then consider Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) Format when N is odd. We give an example where $N = 5$.

```text
AP is Upper                 AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04              00
   11 12 13 14              10 11
      22 23 24              20 21 22
         33 34              30 31 32 33
            44              40 41 42 43 44
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds AP as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid `A(0:4,0:2)` consists of the last three columns of AP upper. The lower triangle `A(3:4,0:1)` consists of the transpose of the first two columns of AP upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid `A(0:4,0:2)` consists of the first three columns of AP lower. The upper triangle `A(0:1,1:2)` consists of the transpose of the last two columns of AP lower. This covers the case N odd and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
02 03 04                00 33 43
12 13 14                10 11 44
22 23 24                20 21 22
00 33 34                30 31 32
01 11 44                40 41 42
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'T'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
02 12 22 00 01             00 10 20 30 40 50
03 13 23 33 11             33 11 21 31 41 51
04 14 24 34 44             43 44 22 32 42 52
```

</section>
